name: A Paris courtyard

place_source.title: Wikidata: Paris (Q90), coordinate location and elevation above sea level

blurb: A stone-walled courtyard garden in central Paris: plane trees and lime trees shade a gravel courtyard with potted figs, climbing ivy and wisteria, visited by sparrows, tits, robins and parakeets by day, and hedgehogs and pipistrelles by night.

facts.text: Paris has a temperate oceanic climate (Köppen Cfb).

source.title: Wikipedia: Paris
source.attribution: Wikipedia contributors, "Paris", English Wikipedia, CC BY-SA 4.0

facts.text: The city's elevation is approximately 48 m above sea level at its public centroid.
Paris hosts a well-established population of rose-ringed parakeets, numbering several thousand individuals.

source.title: Wikipedia: Rose-ringed parakeet
source.attribution: Wikipedia contributors, "Rose-ringed parakeet", English Wikipedia, CC BY-SA 4.0

facts.text: The common pipistrelle is the most abundant bat species in Paris, foraging along tree-lined boulevards and in parks.

source.title: Wikipedia: Common pipistrelle
source.attribution: Wikipedia contributors, "Common pipistrelle", English Wikipedia, CC BY-SA 4.0

facts.text: Common wall lizards thrive on the stone walls and monuments of central Paris.

source.title: Wikipedia: Podarcis muralis
source.attribution: Wikipedia contributors, "Podarcis muralis", English Wikipedia, CC BY-SA 4.0

facts.text: European hedgehogs are present in Paris parks and gardens, though populations have declined in recent decades.
